svg.title: Article 50 versus Article 15: transparency versus accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity
svg.desc: The top lane shows the four Article 50 duties, which apply at any risk level from August 2, 2026. A provider's chatbot tells the person that it is an AI system. A provider's generator marks its output in a machine-readable way so a detector can recognize it. A deployer of emotion recognition informs the people exposed to it. A deployer that publishes a deepfake labels it as AI-generated. The bottom lane shows Article 15, which applies only to high-risk systems: the provider declares accuracy levels and metrics in the instructions for use, builds in redundancy and a fail-safe so faults do not cause harm, protects the model against data poisoning and adversarial inputs, and shows all of this in a conformity assessment before the system is placed on the market.
svg.text: Article 50 versus Article 15: transparency versus accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity
Article 50: tell people about AI and mark AI output
Providers and deployers, at any risk level. Applies from August 2, 2026.
Article 15: build a high-risk system to work well and resist attack
The provider, high-risk systems only. Applies from December 2, 2027 (Annex III) and August 2, 2028 (Annex I).
